title: Credit Standing and the Window a Catering Agreement's Cancellation Record Is Read Over
content:
How far back the cancellation charges already raised on a Corporate Catering Service Agreement are counted turns on how the agreement stands with the accounts office on the day notice is given.

**Where an amount stands unsettled on the agreement**, those charges are counted over the 12 months ending on the day notice is given.

**Where no amount stands unsettled and a payment entry stands on the agreement in the 3 months ending on that day**, they are counted over the 6 months ending on that day.

**Otherwise**, they are counted over the 3 months ending on that day.

| Amount standing unsettled on the agreement | A payment entry in the 3 months ending on the day notice is given | Window the cancellation charges are counted over |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Some amount stands unsettled | either way | 12 months |
| Nothing stands unsettled | yes | 6 months |
| Nothing stands unsettled | no | 3 months |

The first branch is decided on the unsettled amount alone: an agreement carrying an unsettled balance is read over 12 months whether or not a payment entry stands in the last 3 months. The payment window of 3 months and the counting window of 3 months on the third branch are separate figures that happen to carry the same number of months: one is the window a payment entry is looked for in, the other the window the charges are counted over.

By way of illustration, a hypothetical agreement carrying nothing unsettled, with a payment entry recorded 2 months before the day notice is given, has its cancellation charges counted over the 6 months ending on that day; had that payment entry been recorded 4 months before that day, and nothing else since, they would be counted over the 3 months ending on that day.
